why: A reproduction of ci-86, deliberately: every parameter below is the one ci-86 ran, so this turn should land on the same numbers to the digit. ci-86 was the first run played with the baseline of ADR 0048 (its own alpha at 10000, clipped to the range a return can take) and it moved the value policy from 0.10125 to 0.29625 against Greedy and from 0.210 to 0.4975 against search-4, with baselineR2 landing on the 0.1053 the ADR predicted. That is the largest move a value policy has made and it rests on a single run, so it gets confirmed before anything is built on it. What to check: 0.29625 against Greedy, 0.4975 against search-4, 0.6275 against Random, baselineR2 0.1053, advantageStd 0.3852, and the clone refused again at 0.5 against models/clone/ci-69. What is not claimed: 0.4975 is not parity with search-4 -- search-4 beats Greedy 0.930 and this policy loses to Greedy measurably, the fourth non-transitive matchup in this journal. The policy stalls: 23.8 rounds and 56.0% of matches at the cap against search-4, where ADR 0011 gives a capped match to the healthier team. Open after this: the lambda sweep (1.0, 0.95, 0.9, 0.8, 0.5) was walked entirely against the broken baseline, so 0.95 is the best point on a curve that no longer exists and is worth walking again; and the nonlinear baseline ADR 0048 left on the table (0.1215 by gradient boosting, and the engine never reads it).
